answer: Each agent must escrow scarce tokens before joining a market, then earn access to larger trades only after completing tasks whose results are checked by independent agents. A fake identity can claim a share of rewards, but it must lock more tokens and repeat the same costly work; splitting one identity into a pearl, a raven, and a beacon does not multiply verified output. Sybils therefore tie up capital and compute without creating proportionate influence, while honest agents recover their stake through useful work.
